overview:
Coronary artery disease is a common type of heart disease that affects the coronary arteries. In CAD, there is reduced blood flow to the heart muscle. A buildup of fats, cholesterol and other substances in and on the artery walls, called atherosclerosis, usually causes coronary artery disease. The buildup, called plaque, makes the arteries narrow. Coronary artery disease often develops over many years. Symptoms are from the lack of blood flow to the heart. A complete blockage of blood flow can cause a heart attack.
Treatment for coronary artery disease may include medicines and surgery. Eating a nutritious diet, getting regular exercise and not smoking can help prevent coronary artery disease and the conditions that can cause it. Coronary artery disease also may be called coronary heart disease.

less_common: brief or sharp pain in the neck arm or back
symptoms worsening or becoming more frequent
red_flags: chest pain with pressure tightness squeezing or aching
pain or discomfort spreading to shoulder arm back neck jaw teeth or upper belly
heart attack symptoms without chest pain
heart attack symptoms that seem unrelated in women elderly or people with diabetes

causes: plaque buildup in coronary artery walls
plaque rupture causing a blood clot
risk_factors: amount of sleep too little or too much

history_questions: When did you begin having symptoms?
Have the symptoms gotten worse over time?
Do you have chest pain or difficulty breathing?
What does the chest pain feel like?
Does exercise or activity make symptoms worse?
Does anyone in your family have a heart condition or high blood pressure?
Have you been diagnosed with other health conditions?
How much do you exercise in a typical week?
What is your usual daily diet?
Do you or did you smoke? How much? If you quit, when?
Do you drink alcohol? How much?

goals: reduce plaque buildup and improve blood flow
lifestyle: do not smoke or use tobacco
limit sugar salt and saturated fats
eat fruits vegetables and whole grains
eat one or two servings of fish per week
check blood sugar if you have diabetes
medications: cholesterol medicines including statins niacin fibrates and bile acid sequestrants

prevention: do not smoke or use tobacco
limit or do not drink alcohol
control blood pressure cholesterol and diabetes
eat a low-fat low-salt diet rich in fruits vegetables and whole grains
get 7 to 9 hours of sleep daily
when_to_seek_help: high risk of coronary artery disease needing evaluation

followup_questions.chest_pain: Do you have chest pain or chest pressure?
followup_questions.angina: Do you feel squeezing pressure heaviness tightness or pain in the chest?
followup_questions.shortness_of_breath: Do you feel short of breath?
followup_questions.pain_radiation: Does the pain spread to your shoulder arm back neck jaw teeth or upper belly?
followup_questions.cold_sweats: Have you had cold sweats with symptoms?
followup_questions.lightheadedness: Have you felt lightheaded or suddenly dizzy?
followup_questions.hypertension: Have you been diagnosed with high blood pressure?
followup_questions.high_cholesterol: Have you been told you have high cholesterol?
followup_questions.smoking_status: Do you smoke or use tobacco?
followup_questions.obesity: Has a clinician told you that you have obesity?
followup_questions.family_history_heart_disease: Does anyone in your family have heart disease at an early age?
followup_questions.exercise_level: How much do you exercise in a typical week?
followup_questions.diet: What is your usual daily diet?
followup_questions.sleep_duration: How many hours of sleep do you get each night?
followup_questions.alcohol_use: Do you drink alcohol? How much?
followup_questions.stress_level: How much stress do you have in your daily life?

source_notes: Coronary artery disease is caused by plaque buildup that narrows coronary arteries
Symptoms may be absent at first and can occur with exertion or strong emotions
A complete blockage can cause a heart attack

Risk factors include age, birth sex, family history, smoking, high blood pressure, cholesterol problems, diabetes, obesity, chronic kidney disease, inactivity, stress, unhealthy diet, alcohol use, and sleep duration
Obstructive sleep apnea can raise CAD risk
High hs-CRP, high triglycerides, and high homocysteine are possible risk factors
Preeclampsia and other pregnancy complications can increase later CAD risk
Autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and lupus increase atherosclerosis risk
